## 5.2 Interpreting the composition difference (ΔC)

Our approach asks a single question, whether a district's shape changes who it
represents. Rather than judging a district by how irregular it looks, it compares the
composition of the actual district to the composition of a compact reference version of
that same district. The reference can be the convex hull, the minimum bounding circle,
or the compact population center. The metric is the difference between the two
compositions.

$$\Delta C = C_{district} - C_{reference}$$

Here $C_{district}$ is the minority percentage inside the actual district and
$C_{reference}$ is the minority percentage inside the compact reference shape. A subscript
names the reference shape, so $\Delta C_{hull}$, $\Delta C_{mbc}$, and $\Delta C_{cpc}$ apply
this formula to the convex hull, the minimum bounding circle, and the compact population
center (in code `chDiff`, `mbcDiff`, and `cpcDiff`). When precinct data is present a
superscript $v$ marks the version computed on the focal party vote, so $\Delta C_{hull}^{v}$,
$\Delta C_{mbc}^{v}$, and $\Delta C_{cpc}^{v}$ (in code `chDiffV`, `mbcDiffV`, and `cpcDiffV`).
The sign carries the direction, a positive $\Delta C$ toward concentration and a negative one
toward dilution. We use concentration and dilution as neutral terms for the direction, and reserve
packing and cracking for districts with clear evidence of gerrymandering.

There are three cases to read. When $\Delta C$ is strongly positive, the actual district
holds a higher share of the group than its compact reference, which we call concentration.
This may indicate packing where the district is already majority-minority and the group is
over-represented relative to the compact shape. When $\Delta C$ is strongly negative, the
actual district holds a lower share than its compact reference, which we call dilution, and
which may indicate cracking or the exclusion of nearby group members. When $\Delta C$ is close to zero, the
irregular shape does not meaningfully change the group's composition, so the district may
look non-compact while its shape does not appear to distort racial or partisan
representation.

In the figures that follow, the reading is based on the distance between the actual
district (the black point) and the compact-shape estimates. The black point to the right
of the others points toward concentration, and to the left points toward dilution. As you read
the table and figures, consider which districts show the largest gap between the actual
composition and the compact-shape composition, which appear potentially concentrated, which
appear potentially diluted, and which stay similar across all geometries.

## 5.3 Composition by district and reference shape

Figure \@ref(fig:figure-composition) has one panel per district. Within a panel, the row labeled Minority Population (%) is the
racial or ethnic composition, and the row labeled Focal Party Vote (%) is the partisan
composition. Minority Population is the share of the `r basis_word` that belongs to the
group set by `params$group`. Focal Party Vote is the share of the two-party vote for the
chosen office won by the focal party. The vote row appears only when precinct data is
loaded.

Each row carries four points, one for the actual district and one for each compact reference
shape. Black dots are the composition of the actual district. Green dots are the composition
inside its convex hull. Purple dots are the composition inside its minimum bounding circle. Orange
dots are the composition inside its compact population center. The distance from the black dot to
each colored dot is that reference's ΔC.

To read it, go left to right along each row. When the black point sits to the right of the
colored points, the actual district holds more of the group than its compact references, which
points to concentration. When it sits to the left, the district holds less, which points to dilution.
When it sits on top of the colored points, the shape barely changes the composition. When
the colored points fall on both sides of the black point, the three methods disagree, so read that
district with care. The dashed lines mark margin bands around a majority, a tight one at 47.5 and 52.5 percent and a wider one at 45 and 55 percent, so a district inside them is close to even and only outside is the majority clear. We do not print the ΔC
numbers on the plot to keep it readable, so read the exact values from the ΔC table above.

```{r figure-composition, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.height = max(6, 1.5 * n_districts), fig.width = 10, fig.cap = paste0("Composition by district and reference shape, ", params$state, ".")}
combined <- districts_results |> st_drop_geometry() |>
  dplyr::select(DISTRICT, actual = pctMinoritybg, hull = chPct, mbc = mbcPct, cpc = cpcPct) |>
  mutate(type = "Minority Population (%)")
if (have_votes)
  combined <- bind_rows(combined,
    districts_results |> st_drop_geometry() |>
      dplyr::select(DISTRICT, actual = pctMP, hull = chPctV, mbc = mbcPctV, cpc = cpcPctV) |>
      mutate(type = "Focal Party Vote (%)"))
combined <- combined |>
  mutate(DISTRICT = factor(DISTRICT, levels = sort(unique(districts_results$DISTRICT))),
         type = factor(type, levels = c("Minority Population (%)", "Focal Party Vote (%)")))

# long form so the reference type becomes a legend (color + shape), open shapes stay
# readable where points overlap
combined_long <- combined |>
  pivot_longer(c(actual, hull, mbc, cpc), names_to = "reference", values_to = "pct") |>
  mutate(reference = factor(reference, levels = c("actual", "hull", "mbc", "cpc"),
                            labels = c("Actual district", "Convex hull",
                                       "Min. bounding circle", "Compact pop. center")))

ggplot(combined_long, aes(x = pct, y = type, color = reference, shape = reference)) + xlim(0, 100) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(45, 55), color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.6, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(47.5, 52.5), color = "grey35", linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 3.8, stroke = 1.3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Actual district" = "#222222", "Convex hull" = "#3E9B63",
                                "Min. bounding circle" = "#7D3C98", "Compact pop. center" = "#D98400"),
                     name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Actual district" = 1, "Convex hull" = 2,
                                "Min. bounding circle" = 0, "Compact pop. center" = 5),
                     name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ DISTRICT, ncol = 1, labeller = label_both) +
  labs(x = "Percentage (%)", y = NULL,
       caption = "Dashed grey lines mark margin bands around a 50% majority, tight at 47.5 to 52.5 and wide at 45 to 55.") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 15) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, color = "grey35"))
```

## 5.4 Composition difference (ΔC) by district

We show the ΔC two ways, first as bars for the exact size and ranking, then as maps for the
spatial pattern.

### 5.4.1 ΔC bar chart by district and reference shape

Each bar in `r if (have_votes) "Figures \\@ref(fig:figure-cdiff-bars-party) and \\@ref(fig:figure-cdiff-bars-race)" else "Figure \\@ref(fig:figure-cdiff-bars-race)"` is one district's ΔC. Bars to the right are concentration and bars to the left are
dilution. The three panels are the three reference shapes, in the same order and colors as the
composition figure above. Districts are sorted by convex hull ΔC, so the most packed sit at
the top and the most cracked at the bottom. `r if (have_votes) "The partisan version comes first and the racial version below it." else "Only the racial version is shown, because no precinct data is loaded."` A packed
district shows a right-pointing bar in every panel, and a cracked district shows a left-pointing
bar in every panel. When a district's bar points right in one panel but left in another, the
reference shapes disagree, which usually means the population is naturally clustered there, so
treat the case with care.

```{r cdiff-bars-setup, include = FALSE}
ord <- districts_results |> st_drop_geometry() |> arrange(chDiff) |> pull(DISTRICT)

make_cdiff_bars <- function(dcols, ttl) {
  tab <- districts_results |> st_drop_geometry() |> dplyr::select(DISTRICT, dplyr::all_of(dcols))
  names(tab)[2:4] <- c("Convex Hull", "Min. Bounding Circle", "Compact Pop. Center")
  tab |>
    pivot_longer(-DISTRICT, names_to = "reference", values_to = "Cdiff") |>
    mutate(DISTRICT = factor(DISTRICT, levels = ord),
           reference = factor(reference, levels = c("Convex Hull", "Min. Bounding Circle", "Compact Pop. Center")),
           direction = ifelse(Cdiff >= 0, "Concentration", "Dilution")) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = Cdiff, y = DISTRICT, fill = direction)) +
    geom_col() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey35", linewidth = 0.6) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Concentration" = "#DC6D85", "Dilution" = "#6EA6C3")) +
    facet_wrap(~ reference, labeller = as_labeller(ref_labels)) +
    labs(x = "ΔC (percentage points)", y = "District", fill = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 15) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          strip.text = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 15, face = "bold"))
}
```

```{r figure-cdiff-bars-party, echo = FALSE, eval = have_votes, fig.height = max(5, 0.9 * n_districts), fig.width = 11, fig.cap = paste0("ΔC by district for the ", fp_disp, " vote, by reference shape, ", params$state, ".")}
make_cdiff_bars(c("chDiffV", "mbcDiffV", "cpcDiffV"),
                paste0("ΔC by district, focal party vote (", params$state, ")"))
```

```{r figure-cdiff-bars-race, echo = FALSE, fig.height = max(5, 0.9 * n_districts), fig.width = 11, fig.cap = paste0("ΔC by district for the ", params$group, " ", basis_word, ", by reference shape, ", params$state, ".")}
make_cdiff_bars(c("chDiff", "mbcDiff", "cpcDiff"),
                paste0("ΔC by district, ", params$group, " population (", params$state, ")"))
```

### 5.4.2 ΔC choropleth map by district

`r if (have_votes) "Figures \\@ref(fig:figure-cdiff-map-party) and \\@ref(fig:figure-cdiff-map-race)" else "Figure \\@ref(fig:figure-cdiff-map-race)"` draw the same ΔC on the district map, so the spatial pattern is visible. Each district is
shaded by its ΔC, red for concentration and blue for dilution, with each district number labeled. The
three panels are the three reference shapes, side by side, in the same order as the bar chart. `r if (have_votes) "As with the bars, the partisan map comes first and the racial map below it." else "Only the racial map is shown, because no precinct data is loaded."` To read it, find a district by its number and compare
its color across the three panels. A district that is red in all three panels is robustly concentrated,
and one that is blue in all three is robustly diluted. A district that changes color between
panels is a case where the choice of reference shape matters.

```{r cdiff-map-setup, include = FALSE}
make_cdiff_map <- function(dcols, ttl) {
  tab <- districts_results |> st_drop_geometry() |> dplyr::select(DISTRICT, dplyr::all_of(dcols))
  names(tab)[2:4] <- c("Convex Hull", "Min. Bounding Circle", "Compact Pop. Center")
  tab <- tab |>
    pivot_longer(-DISTRICT, names_to = "reference", values_to = "Cdiff") |>
    mutate(reference = factor(reference, levels = c("Convex Hull", "Min. Bounding Circle", "Compact Pop. Center")))
  m <- districts |> dplyr::select(DISTRICT) |> left_join(tab, by = "DISTRICT")
  lim <- max(abs(m$Cdiff), na.rm = TRUE)   # symmetric color range
  ggplot(m) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = Cdiff), color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
    # district number on top, signed ΔC below it: a positive (red) value is
    # concentration and a negative (blue) value is dilution, read per district and panel
    geom_sf_text(aes(label = paste0(DISTRICT, "\n",
                     ifelse(is.na(Cdiff), "", sprintf("%+.1f", Cdiff)))),
                 size = 3.8, fontface = "bold", color = "grey10", lineheight = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#6EA6C3", mid = "white", high = "#DC6D85",
                         midpoint = 0, limits = c(-lim, lim),
                         breaks  = c(-lim, 0, lim),
                         labels  = c("Dilution", "0", "Concentration"),
                         name = "ΔC") +
    facet_wrap(~ reference, ncol = 3, labeller = as_labeller(ref_labels)) +
    # horizontal colorbar along the bottom, so the "Dilution"/"Concentration" end
    # labels are not clipped in wide, short states
    guides(fill = guide_colorbar(title.position = "left", title.vjust = 0.9,
                                 barwidth = unit(9, "cm"), barheight = unit(0.5, "cm"))) +
    theme_void(base_size = 18) +
    theme(strip.text = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 20, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 6)),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.title = element_text(size = 18),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 16))
}
```

```{r figure-cdiff-map-party, echo = FALSE, eval = have_votes, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 4 * map_asp + 2.0, fig.cap = paste0("ΔC mapped for the ", fp_disp, " vote, by reference shape, ", params$state, ".")}
make_cdiff_map(c("chDiffV", "mbcDiffV", "cpcDiffV"),
               paste0("ΔC by district, focal party vote (", params$state, ")"))
```
